summary: Milestone 2026.07.525 completed 12 experiments in 40.0 minutes, including 4 compute-bound experiments. The 31.8-minute three-family synthesis entry dominated the recorded tail, but the bounded timing does not separate dependency wait, setup, model loading, inference, or verification.
bottlenecks_identified: The 31.8-minute compute-bound three-family synthesis entry had a recorded duration equal to 79.5% of total milestone wall time.
Task-level timing cannot attribute the 31.8-minute synthesis or 6.91-minute repair durations to dependency wait, fixture preparation, model loading, inference, or verification.
The supplied data does not record whether the three-family work loaded models concurrently, so runner-selection efficiency cannot be diagnosed.
improvements_suggested: Record phase timers for dependency readiness, fixture preparation, model loading, inference, verification, and artifact writing on every compute-bound task.
Correlate GPU utilization samples and runner selection with each compute-bound task's start and end so an idle monitor snapshot cannot be mistaken for task-lifetime utilization.
Add an explicit model-concurrency declaration to scheduling and select DualGPURunner only when at least two models are intentionally loaded in parallel.
Cache validated fixture and retrieval inputs by checksum so later gated arms can reuse them when their declared inputs match.
top_3_highest_leverage_actions: Instrument the 31.8-minute three-family path with phase-level timers before the next run.
Emit task-linked GPU and runner-selection telemetry for every compute-bound launch.
Dispatch DualGPURunner conditionally when the scheduler declares at least two parallel model loads.
meta_reflection: The data ranks the operational tail but does not explain it causally, and the idle GPU snapshot is not task-correlated. A nonzero savings forecast or a claim that a parallel-model DualGPURunner opportunity was missed would exceed the supplied evidence.
